import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA: all numeric constants for the problem instance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    "mills": ["M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7", "M8", "M9", "M10"],
    "customers": [f"C{j}" for j in range(1, 1001)],
    "paper_types": ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"],
    "machines": ["L1", "L2", "L3"],
    "materials": ["m1", "m2", "m3", "m4"],

    # D[j,k]: monthly demand of customer j for paper type k
    "D": {(j, k): 10.0
          for j in [f"C{j}" for j in range(1, 1001)]
          for k in ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"]},

    # r[k,l,m]: raw material m needed per unit of paper k on machine l
    "r": {(k, l, m): 1.0
          for k in ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"]
          for l in ["L1", "L2", "L3"]
          for m in ["m1", "m2", "m3", "m4"]},

    # R[i,m]: monthly availability of raw material m at mill i
    "R": {(i, m): 1.0e7
          for i in ["M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7", "M8", "M9", "M10"]
          for m in ["m1", "m2", "m3", "m4"]},

    # c[k,l]: machine time per unit of paper k on machine l
    "c_prod": {(k, l): 1.0
               for k in ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"]
               for l in ["L1", "L2", "L3"]},

    # c[i,l]: monthly machine time available at mill i for machine l
    "c_avail": {(i, l): 1.0e7
                for i in ["M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7", "M8", "M9", "M10"]
                for l in ["L1", "L2", "L3"]},

    # P[i,k,l]: production cost per unit of paper k on machine l at mill i
    "P": {(i, k, l): 5.0
          for i in ["M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7", "M8", "M9", "M10"]
          for k in ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"]
          for l in ["L1", "L2", "L3"]},

    # T[i,j,k]: transport cost per unit of paper k from mill i to customer j
    "T": {(i, j, k): 1.0
          for i in ["M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7", "M8", "M9", "M10"]
          for j in [f"C{j}" for j in range(1, 1001)]
          for k in ["K1", "K2", "K3", "K4", "K5"]},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    mills = d["mills"]
    customers = d["customers"]
    paper_types = d["paper_types"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    materials = d["materials"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ------------------- Sets -------------------
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=mills, ordered=True)
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=customers, ordered=True)
    model.K = pyo.Set(initialize=paper_types, ordered=True)
    model.L = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=materials, ordered=True)

    # ------------------- Variables -------------------
    # produce[i,k,l]: units of paper k made on machine l at mill i
    model.produce = pyo.Var(model.I, model.K, model.L,
                            domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ship[i,j,k]: units of paper k shipped from mill i to customer j
    model.ship = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, model.K,
                         domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ------------------- Objective -------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        prod_cost = sum(d["P"][(i, k, l)] * m.produce[i, k, l]
                        for i in m.I for k in m.K for l in m.L)
        trans_cost = sum(d["T"][(i, j, k)] * m.ship[i, j, k]
                         for i in m.I for j in m.J for k in m.K)
        return prod_cost + trans_cost

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ------------------- Constraints -------------------

    # Raw material availability at each mill
    def raw_material_rule(m, i, mat):
        return sum(d["r"][(k, l, mat)] * m.produce[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K for l in m.L) <= d["R"][(i, mat)]

    model.raw_material = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.M,
                                        rule=raw_material_rule)

    # Machine time availability at each mill
    def machine_time_rule(m, i, l):
        return sum(d["c_prod"][(k, l)] * m.produce[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K) <= d["c_avail"][(i, l)]

    model.machine_time = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.L,
                                        rule=machine_time_rule)

    # Customer demand must be exactly satisfied
    def demand_rule(m, j, k):
        return sum(m.ship[i, j, k] for i in m.I) == d["D"][(j, k)]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.J, model.K, rule=demand_rule)

    # Flow balance: total shipped out of mill i of paper k equals total produced
    def balance_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(m.ship[i, j, k] for j in m.J) == \
               sum(m.produce[i, k, l] for l in m.L)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "I": 10,      # number of mills
    "J": 1000,    # number of customers
    "L": 3,       # number of machine types
    "M": 4,       # number of raw materials
    "K": 5,       # number of paper types

    # D[(j,k)] : customer j requires D units of paper type k each month
    # (first customer shown; others default)
    "D": {(0, 0): 500.0, (0, 1): 300.0, (0, 2): 400.0,
          (0, 3): 250.0, (0, 4): 350.0},

    # r[(k,l,m)] : amount of material m to produce one unit of paper type k on machine l
    "r": {(0, 0, 0): 0.5, (0, 0, 1): 0.2, (0, 0, 2): 0.1, (0, 0, 3): 0.0,
          (0, 1, 0): 0.5, (0, 1, 1): 0.2, (0, 1, 2): 0.1, (0, 1, 3): 0.0},
    "r_default": 0.2,

    # R[(i,m)] : material m available monthly at mill i
    "R": {(0, 0): 100000.0, (0, 1): 50000.0,
          (0, 2): 30000.0, (0, 3): 20000.0},
    "R_default": 50000.0,

    # c_kl[(k,l)] : machine time to produce one unit of paper type k on machine l
    "c_kl": {(0, 0): 0.1, (0, 1): 0.08, (0, 2): 0.12},
    "c_kl_default": 0.1,

    # c_il[(i,l)] : machine time available monthly at mill i for machine type l
    "c_il": {(0, 0): 4000.0, (0, 1): 3000.0, (0, 2): 3500.0},
    "c_il_default": 4000.0,

    # P[(i,k,l)] : production cost per unit
    "P": {(0, 0, 0): 2.5, (0, 0, 1): 2.7, (0, 0, 2): 2.4},
    "P_default": 2.5,

    # T[(i,j,k)] : transport cost per unit
    "T": {(0, 0, 0): 1.2},
    "T_default": 1.5,
}

# ---- default demand so all 1000 customers get a requirement -------------
for jj in range(1, DATA["J"]):
    for kk in range(DATA["K"]):
        DATA["D"].setdefault((jj, kk), 10.0)


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- Sets ----
    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["I"] - 1)          # mills
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["J"] - 1)          # customers
    model.L = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["L"] - 1)          # machines
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["M"] - 1)          # materials
    model.K = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["K"] - 1)          # paper types

    # ---- Decision variables ----
    # x[i,k,l] : units of paper type k produced on machine l at mill i
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, model.K, model.L,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # y[i,j,k] : units of paper type k shipped from mill i to customer j
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, model.K,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- Objective: minimize production + transportation cost ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        prod = sum(d["P"].get((i, k, l), d["P_default"]) * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for i in m.I for k in m.K for l in m.L)
        ship = sum(d["T"].get((i, j, k), d["T_default"]) * m.y[i, j, k]
                   for i in m.I for j in m.J for k in m.K)
        return prod + ship

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- (a) Raw material availability per mill per material ----
    def mat_rule(m, i, mm):
        return sum(d["r"].get((k, l, mm), d["r_default"]) * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K for l in m.L) <= d["R"].get((i, mm), d["R_default"])

    model.raw_mat = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.M, rule=mat_rule)

    # ---- (b) Machine time availability per mill per machine type ----
    def mch_rule(m, i, l):
        return sum(d["c_kl"].get((k, l), d["c_kl_default"]) * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K) <= d["c_il"].get((i, l), d["c_il_default"])

    model.machine_time = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.L, rule=mch_rule)

    # ---- (c) Balance: everything produced at mill i of paper k is shipped out ----
    def bal_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for j in m.J) == sum(m.x[i, k, l] for l in m.L)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=bal_rule)

    # ---- (d) Demand: each customer's requirement of each paper type is met ----
    def dem_rule(m, j, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for i in m.I) == d["D"].get((j, k), 0.0)

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.J, model.K, rule=dem_rule)

    return model

    model.y = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.J, model.K,

    )

    def raw_material_rule(m, i, mm):

    # (d) Supply balance: shipped <= produced per mill & paper type
    def supply_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for j in m.J) <= sum(m.x[i, l, k] for l in m.L)
    model.supply = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=supply_rule)

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["T"][i][j][k] * m.y[i, j, k]
            for i in m.I for j in m.J for k in m.K
        )
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# PROBLEM: Multi-mill, multi-machine, multi-product production + distribution
#
# SETS / INDICES
#   I = mills            (10)
#   J = customers        (1000)
#   L = machine types    (3)
#   M = raw materials    (4)
#   K = paper types      (5)
#
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   x[i,k,l] >= 0 : units of paper type k produced on machine l at mill i
#   y[i,j,k] >= 0 : units of paper type k shipped from mill i to customer j
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize)
#   total production cost  +  total transportation cost
#     sum_{i,k,l} P[i,k,l] * x[i,k,l]  +  sum_{i,j,k} T[i,j,k] * y[i,j,k]
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Raw material availability at each mill:
#         sum_{k,l} r[m,k,l] * x[i,k,l] <= R[i,m]      for all i, m
#   (2) Machine time availability at each mill:
#         sum_{k} c[k,l] * x[i,k,l] <= c_il[i,l]       for all i, l
#   (3) Customer demand satisfaction:
#         sum_{i} y[i,j,k] = D[j,k]                    for all j, k
#   (4) Flow balance: everything shipped from a mill must have been produced:
#         sum_{j} y[i,j,k] = sum_{l} x[i,k,l]          for all i, k
# =============================================================================

    # T[i,j,k] : transport cost per unit of paper k from mill i to customer j
    "T": {},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---------------- Sets ----------------
    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["n_mills"] - 1)
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["n_customers"] - 1)
    model.L = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["n_machines"] - 1)
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["n_materials"] - 1)
    model.K = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["n_papers"] - 1)

    # ---------------- Decision variables ----------------
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, model.K, model.L,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, model.K,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---------------- Objective ----------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        prod = sum(d["P"][(i, k, l)] * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for i in m.I for k in m.K for l in m.L)
        trans = sum(d["T"][(i, j, k)] * m.y[i, j, k]
                    for i in m.I for j in m.J for k in m.K)
        return prod + trans

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---------------- Constraint (1): raw material availability ----------------
    def raw_material_rule(m, i, mat):
        return sum(d["r"][(mat, k, l)] * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K for l in m.L) <= d["R"][(i, mat)]

    model.raw_material = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.M,
                                        rule=raw_material_rule)

    # ---------------- Constraint (2): machine time availability ----------------
    def machine_time_rule(m, i, l):
        return sum(d["c"][(k, l)] * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K) <= d["c_il"][(i, l)]

    model.machine_time = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.L,
                                        rule=machine_time_rule)

    # ---------------- Constraint (3): customer demand satisfaction ----------------
    def demand_rule(m, j, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for i in m.I) == d["D"][(j, k)]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.J, model.K, rule=demand_rule)

    # ---------------- Constraint (4): production / shipment balance ----------------
    def balance_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for j in m.J) == sum(m.x[i, k, l]
                                                     for l in m.L)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

    # y[i,j,k]: units of paper type k shipped from mill i to customer j
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

                   for i in m.I for k in m.K for l in m.L)
        trans = sum(d["transport_cost"] * m.y[i, j, k]
                    for i in m.I for j in m.J for k in m.K)
        return prod + trans

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    model.raw_material_availability = pyo.Constraint(

    # (b) Machine-time availability at each mill for each machine type
    #     sum_k c_kl * x_ikl <= c_il
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def machine_time_rule(m, i, l):
        return sum(d["machine_time_per_unit"] * m.x[i, k, l]
                   for k in m.K) <= d["machine_time_available"]

        model.I, model.L, rule=machine_time_rule)

    # (c) Customer demand satisfaction: sum_i y_ijk = D_jk
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m, j, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for i in m.I) == \
            d["demand_per_customer_per_type"]

    model.demand_satisfaction = pyo.Constraint(
        model.J, model.K, rule=demand_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (d) Flow balance: everything produced at mill i of type k is shipped
    #     sum_j y_ijk = sum_l x_ikl
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def balance_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, k] for j in m.J) == \
            sum(m.x[i, k, l] for l in m.L)

    model.flow_balance = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.K, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

  sum_{i,k,l} P[i,k,l] * prod[i,k,l]  +  sum_{i,j,k} T[i,j,k] * ship[i,j,k]

(2) Machine-time availability: "c_{il} - machine time available each month at
    mill i for machine type l" and "c_{kl} - machine time required to produce one
    unit of paper of type k on machine l":

(3) Demand satisfaction: "D_{jk} - customer j requires k units of paper each

        sum_{i} ship[i,j,k] >= D[j,k]                for all j, k
(4) Flow balance (production must cover shipments): every unit shipped from a

def build_model(data=None):

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Sets

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decision variables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.prod = pyo.Var(
        model.MILLS, model.PAPER_TYPES, model.MACHINE_TYPES,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )
    model.ship = pyo.Var(
        model.MILLS, model.CUSTOMERS, model.PAPER_TYPES,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: minimize production + transportation cost
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):

            d["prod_cost"] * m.prod[i, k, l]
            for i in m.MILLS for k in m.PAPER_TYPES for l in m.MACHINE_TYPES
        )
        trans_cost = sum(
            d["trans_cost"] * m.ship[i, j, k]
            for i in m.MILLS for j in m.CUSTOMERS for k in m.PAPER_TYPES
        )
        return prod_cost + trans_cost

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (1) Raw-material availability
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def raw_avail_rule(m, i, mat):
        return sum(
            d["raw_usage"] * m.prod[i, k, l]
            for k in m.PAPER_TYPES for l in m.MACHINE_TYPES
        ) <= d["raw_avail"]

    model.raw_avail = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MILLS, model.RAW_MATERIALS, rule=raw_avail_rule
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (2) Machine-time availability
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def mach_time_rule(m, i, l):
        return sum(
            d["mach_time_req"] * m.prod[i, k, l]
            for k in m.PAPER_TYPES
        ) <= d["mach_time_avail"]

    model.mach_time = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MILLS, model.MACHINE_TYPES, rule=mach_time_rule
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (3) Demand satisfaction
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m, j, k):
        return sum(
            m.ship[i, j, k] for i in m.MILLS
        ) >= d["demand"]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(
        model.CUSTOMERS, model.PAPER_TYPES, rule=demand_rule
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (4) Flow balance: shipments of (i,k) cannot exceed production of (i,k)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def flow_rule(m, i, k):
        return sum(
            m.ship[i, j, k] for j in m.CUSTOMERS
        ) <= sum(
            m.prod[i, k, l] for l in m.MACHINE_TYPES
        )

    model.flow = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MILLS, model.PAPER_TYPES, rule=flow_rule
    )

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, d["num_customers"] - 1)     # customers

                   for k in m.K for l in m.L) \

                                          rule=material_rule)

            == sum(m.x[i, k, l] for l in m.L)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=balance_rule)

    return model
